item.subject: maths
item.stem:
The diagram shows lines $LM$ and $NO$ cut by transversal $BD$. Lalit notes that triangles $LBD$ and $NDB$ are congruent, and that congruence makes a pair of alternate interior angles equal.

Which claim correctly concludes that $LM \parallel NO$?

options.A: $LM \parallel NO$, because the congruent triangles make a pair of alternate interior angles equal for transversal $BD$.
options.B: Lines $LM$ and $NO$ are the alternate interior angles on transversal $BD$.
options.C: $LM \parallel NO$, because the triangles are congruent, even when those alternate interior angles are unequal.
options.D: $LM \parallel NO$, because matching sides of the triangles are equal, and equal sides alone settle parallelism.
